All inputs arrive via MCPAQLHandler.dispatchGatekeeper() which validates params through validateRequiredString() and the MCP-AQL transport layer. Unicode normalization is applied at the MCPAQLHandler entry point before dispatch. This module receives pre-validated params, not raw user input.

WEB-CONSOLE COMPOSITION: Registrar wires stores, modules, and the secured router. Runtime request input is normalized by ConsoleUnicodeNormalization before route handlers; deployment/configuration secrets and OAuth identifiers remain exact-match opaque values.

OPAQUE OAUTH FLOW VALUES: Login state, PKCE verifier, authorization code, session cookies, and JWT values are credentials/protocol values that must be exact-match validated. Return paths are normalized through ConsoleReturnPaths and route payloads pass through ConsoleUnicodeNormalization.

OPAQUE OAUTH CLIENT VALUES: Authorization codes, code verifiers, redirect URIs, and JWTs are protocol credentials and must not be Unicode-folded. JWT claims are validated after jose verification and are not free-form request payloads.

OPERATOR BOOTSTRAP IDENTITY: Admin provisioning keys users by exact OAuth subject identifiers. Normalizing subject strings would break identity binding; display names are free-form and not used for authorization decisions.

AUDIT CONTEXT ONLY: Admin audit events record authenticated session context, route metadata, normalized path/query/body-derived handler summaries, and opaque request headers for traceability. It does not authorize from raw user text.

OPAQUE SESSION VALUES: Session cookies and stored hashes are exact-match credentials and must not be Unicode-normalized. Request path/query/body values are normalized after authentication by the secured router.
OPAQUE CSRF VALUES: CSRF cookie/header values, Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site, and X-Console-Request are browser protocol values checked by exact comparison. They are not free-form user payloads.

NORMALIZED ROUTE PARAM CONSUMER: Ownership checks run after ConsoleUnicodeNormalization and authentication. Runtime session ids are read from normalized route params and compared as exact stored identifiers.

NORMALIZED ROUTE PARAM CONSUMER: Protected-correlation rate limits run after ConsoleUnicodeNormalization and authentication. Account correlation ids are normalized route params before limiter consumption.

Bearer Authorization values are opaque credentials and must be exact-match validated, not Unicode-folded. MCP request payloads are normalized after authentication by StreamableHttpServer/ServerSetup before tool handlers see user content.
Interface contract only for auth providers. Concrete providers validate opaque token strings exactly; payload/user content normalization happens at HTTP/MCP request boundaries after authentication.
Instrumentation decorator for IAuthProvider.validate(). It times provider validation outcomes but does not interpret user content; bearer tokens remain opaque exact-match credentials by design.

Performance-only instrumentation wrapper. Concrete auth providers own TOKEN_VALIDATION_FAILURE audit logging with issuer/key/provider context, and this wrapper intentionally avoids duplicate security events.
SSE tickets are random base64url opaque credentials bound to a stream name and must be exact-match redeemed once. Normalizing ticket values would weaken token comparison semantics.
Build-time ESLint configuration only. Contains rule metadata and file patterns, not production request handling or user-input processing.

EXACT ROUTER BOUNDARY: This assembler installs ConsoleUnicodeNormalization for request targets before every handler and body-key normalization after authentication. Its direct query reads inspect only already-normalized credential-presence keys.

EXACT DCR BOUNDARY: OAuth redirect URIs and protocol identifiers remain byte-exact. Human-visible client_name rejects directional and zero-width characters in dcrPolicy and is NFC-normalized before persistence.

EXACT OIDC BOUNDARY: Interaction IDs, CSRF values, cookies, method IDs, and OAuth query fields are opaque protocol values checked by exact comparison. Human-entered form fields are validated by the selected authentication method.

EXACT AUTHORIZATION-SERVER BOUNDARY: Bearer tokens, OAuth parameters, headers, and signing-key identifiers are opaque exact-match values. The packaged font path is restricted by an ASCII filename allowlist.
EXACT CONSOLE ROUTE MODULE: Provider route parameters arrive through ConsoleUnicodeNormalization and are then restricted by PROVIDER_ID_PATTERN plus the reserved-provider set.

EXACT CONSOLE SERVICE: Requests arrive through the secured normalized console router. Human-visible display_name and category are NFC-normalized and reject directional or zero-width characters; remaining fields receive method-specific validation before persistence.
EXACT CONSOLE SERVICE: Query keys and values arrive through ConsoleUnicodeNormalization, then type, search, page, and page-size fields receive bounded semantic validation.
EXACT CONSOLE ROUTE MODULE: Collection type and name parameters are normalized by ConsoleRouterAssembler before this module performs type checks and dispatches to the service.

EXACT CONSOLE SERVICE: Body keys arrive normalized; the catalog path is bounded and restricted to library paths, then authoritative collection path/content validation runs before portfolio persistence.
EXACT CONSOLE SERVICE: Body keys arrive normalized. Allowlist values use normalizeAllowlistDisplayValue followed by kind-specific validation; notes are bounded and are not authorization identifiers.

EXACT MAGIC-LINK BOUNDARY: Link tokens and CSRF bindings are opaque signed credentials and must not be Unicode-normalized. Email addresses and IP rate-limit keys use their own canonicalization and validation.
EXACT LOCAL-AUTH BOUNDARY: Invite tokens are opaque credentials and passwords must be hashed exactly as entered. Request bodies are capped and all account fields receive method-specific validation.
EXACT GITHUB OAUTH BOUNDARY: Authorization code and state are opaque OAuth values bound to the interaction cookie and verified by exact comparison before exchange.

validate() delegates token verification to EmbeddedASTokens, which now emits TOKEN_VALIDATION_FAILURE events via SecurityMonitor. This wrapper only composes the authorization-server routes and provider facade.

BaseElementManager.validate() delegates to element-specific validators; load/save/delete audit events are emitted by composed element services and subtype hooks. This method is a pure validation facade, not an authorization decision point.

Read-side portfolio projection calls manager.validate() to compute validationStatus only. Console administrative mutations are audit-written by ConsoleSecuredRouterAssembler; element persistence operations retain their own element audit events.
